source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Consider a bandit problem where the set of arms is the unit sphere in $\Real^r$, and $W^{\BF u}_t$ has a standard normal distribution with mean zero and variance one for all $t$ and $\BF u$. If $\BF Z$ has a multivariate normal distribution with mean $\BF 0$ and covariance matrix $\BF I_r / r$, then for all policies $\psi$ and every $T \geq r^2$, ${\rm Risk} \left( T, \psi \right) \geq 0.006 \,r\, \sqrt{T}$.

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Consequently, for any policy $\psi$ and $T \geq r^2$, there exists $\BF z \in \Real^r$ such that ${\rm Regret} \left( \BF z, T, \psi \right) \geq 0.006 \, r \, \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Regret is defined conditionally on Z=z through means: pseudo-regret. Worst case over z (z unbounded norm).

symbols.a_1: positive constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0, J

conditions: Assumption 1: sigma_0-subgaussian noise, arm norms <= u_bar, r linearly independent arms with lambda_min >= lambda_0

source.label: theorem:greedy-regret
source.quote: Suppose that Assumption \ref{assumption:basic} holds and that the sets $\CAL U_r$ satisfy the SBAR($J$) condition. Then, there exists a positive constant $a_1$ that depends only on $\sigma_0$, $\bar{u}$, $\lambda_0$, and $J$, such that for any $\BF z \in \Real^r \setminus \{\BF 0\}$ and $T \geq r$, ${\rm Regret} \left( \BF z, \, T, \, \textsc{PEGE} \right) \leq a_1 \, \left( \norm{\BF z} + \frac{1}{\norm{\BF z}} \right) \, r \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Corollary 3.3 specializes to the unit sphere with standard normal noise with an absolute constant a_3 (same form, not recorded separately). Computation of greedy argmax not discussed.

symbols.a_2: positive constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0, J, M

conditions: E[||Z||] <= M and E[1/||Z||] <= M for every r

source.label: theorem:greedy-regret
source.quote: Suppose in addition, that there exists a constant $M > 0$ such that for every $r\geq 2$ we have $\E \left[\, \norm{\BF Z} \,\right] \leq M$ and $\E \left[ \,1/\norm{\BF Z} \,\right] \leq M$. Then, there exists a positive constant $a_2$ ... such that for any $T \geq r$, ${\rm Risk} \left( T, \, \textsc{PEGE} \right) \leq a_2 \, r \, \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Corollary 3.3 gives the same form for unit sphere with N(0,I/r) prior (matching Theorem 2.1).
